title: Elastic slab zoning + KV airlock: admission-control for stable GPU budgets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce tail OOMs and severe latency spikes during mixed workloads by introducing an 'elastic slab zoning' approach for static weights and a 'KV airlock' admission-control layer for KV/activation pressure. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and canary rollout for a GPU memory controller that enforces bounded budgets for weights/KV/activations and gracefully degrades (admission throttling, quantized fallbacks) under pressure.

Background: Our continuous batching runtime interleaves many tenants and request sizes which leads to sporadic KV growth and activation surges. Existing global soft watermarks allow bursts but cause correlated OOMs under multi-tenant microbursts. We need a controller that: 1) partitions GPU memory into interpretive zones (weight slabs immutable at load time; KV cushion zone elastic; activation ephemeral pool) and 2) gates new batch admissions with a KV airlock that compresses, prefetches, or stalls requests depending on forecasted headroom.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce per-GPU OOM incidents attributed to KV/activation pressure by >= 80% on canary hosts.
- P95 token latency for mixed 0-2048 token requests increases by <= 5% compared to baseline.
- No more than 1% throughput loss for steady-state workloads.
- Accurate headroom forecast within +/-10% for the 30s horizon for 90% of samples.

Proposed approach:
1) Elastic slab zoning: allocate a contiguous weight region at model load as a read-only slab with explicit accounting. Remaining GPU memory is logically divided into two pools: KV cushion (elastic, reclaimable) and activation pool (ephemeral, LIFO-preemptible). Slab zoning enables fast weight residency checks and simplifies eviction precedence.
2) KV airlock: an admission-control interceptor executed at batch enqueue time. For each incoming batch we compute a cheap delta estimate of KV growth + activation peak using a lightweight estimator (per-model distribution sketches for prefix lengths, per-tenant average KV/change factors). The airlock has three actions: ALLOW (admit), COMPRESS-AND-ALLOW (apply aggressive KV compression/quantization or KV-rollover to disk), STALL-OR-FALLBACK (return quantized model variant, or reject/queue request).
3) Headroom forecaster: rolling quantile estimator using exponential histograms per host that predicts usable memory headroom at horizons 10s/30s/60s. Forecast guide works with admission-control thresholds tuned for latency SLOs and burst absorbency.
4) Preemption policy: activations are first preemptible; KV is reclaimed next (with graceful serialization of cached entries); weights are never evicted while in active slab. If reclaiming fails, fallback routes to quantized model variant or remote-host execution.

Instrumentation & metrics: track per-GPU: reserved_weight_bytes, kv_bytes, activation_peak_bytes, forecast_headroom, admitted_batches, airlock_action_counts, stall_rate, fallback_rate, OOM_count, tail_latency_token_50/95/99. Existing trace hooks will be extended to label airlock decisions for per-tenant analysis.

Rollout plan:
- Prototype: implement elastic slab zoning accounting and simple airlock estimator in staging (unit tests + microbench).
- Perf bench: run 72h mixed-workload replay comparing baseline vs. controller (canary hosts identical hw).
- Canary: enable on 5% of serving fleet with conservative thresholds and monitor OOM and latency.
- Ramp: increase to 25% after 72h stable; 100% after 2 cycles of verification and stakeholder sign-off.

Risks & mitigation:
- Over-eager admission control could significantly increase tail latency by stalling: mitigate by conservative initial thresholds and COMPRESS-AND-ALLOW option.
- Compression/quantization code paths may have correctness regressions; use model regression tests and golden outputs for top-10 customer models.
- Forecast inaccuracy under novel workloads; add fallback to short-term conservative static reserve if forecast confidence low.

Dependencies: kernel async-eviction hooks, quantized-variant runtime route, console dashboards for new metrics, canary fleet allocation.

Deliverables: design doc (Confluence link), prototype PR, perf benchmark report, canary rollout runbook, dashboard panels, incident playbook for OOMs related to airlock decisions.
